features: TASK_DAG_V1 dependency validation and READY states
candidate-bound post-patch challenge on a different worker slot

toolSchema.interpretation: The dependency and lease contract materially enlarges only the advanced batch schema; the normal fast path remains near its 0.6.4 size.

issuesFoundByTelemetryReview: Width changed to two at 0ms although only the owner was READY.
The explicit challenge kind was reported as inspect.
candidateCorrection.resolution: The widening trigger now requires independent READY capacity or candidate-thread isolation; explicit node kinds take precedence. Both received focused regressions and a new real run.

issues: A challenge could reuse the producer slot when its alternate slot was still occupied by a sibling.
The throughput schema allowed 1/2/4/8 while runtime still applied legacy speed-first 4/8 validation.
Candidate dependency evidence still included the producer summary and evidence despite the clean-room contract.
prepublishCorrection.resolution: The producer slot is ineligible for its candidate challenge; throughput has independent 1/2/4/8 validation; candidate input contains only producer completion state and fingerprint metadata. Worker-returned blocked state also propagates without being relabelled failed.
regressions: candidate challenge waits when only its producer slot is idle
a worker-blocked node remains blocked and blocks its descendants
candidate dependency evidence omits producer reasoning

previousCorrectedDagRun.interpretation: The repeated graph passed both times, while challenge duration varied materially.

matchedBroadReadOnly.interpretation: Both routes opened all four slots at 0ms and used the same node order. The observed adaptive arm was faster but more expensive; one sample cannot causally attribute either difference to routing rather than model/output variance.

limitations: Progressive widening is event-driven; four independent READY nodes widen to four immediately.
No straggler hedge or speculative duplicate is shipped, so one long node still controls p95 wall time.
Chained writers are rejected because successor worktrees cannot inherit unintegrated predecessor patches safely.
Child-task suggestions, Terra counsel, learning-based routing, false acceptance, duplicate exploration, result use, and route regret remain unavailable.
Each live benchmark arm has n=1 and is evidence for an alpha, not a universal performance claim.
